# The Endpoint Response Merge Is Not Generated by Known Local Source Moves

## Status

This falsifier remains correct for unary-factorized local moves, but its open
gap is closed by atomic simultaneous inversion of both nonrepeated generators.
That coupled move is legal even though either unary inversion is illegal.

## Falsified conjecture

The natural conjecture was that the three framing states were exactly the
connected components generated by local response-invisible presentation
changes.

This is false.

## Exact result

On the thirty-two legal signed presentations, admit the following typed partial
moves only when the resulting presentation remains Moore-legal:

- endpoint reversal;
- exchange of the two nonrepeated slots;
- reversal of the repeated-generator sign;
- either tail-sign reversal on the endpoint stratum;
- simultaneous tail-sign reversal on the through stratum.

Every admitted edge preserves the framing classifier. Their generated
groupoid has four components of size eight:

\[
E_0,\qquad E_1,\qquad T_+,\qquad T_-.
\]

The reflection response has only three fibers because it identifies the two
endpoint components:

\[
E_0\sim_R E_1,\qquad T_+\not\sim_R T_-.
\]

Thus the through-going split is locally constructed by polarity, but the
endpoint merge is not generated by any tested local source move.

## Meaning

Equality of endpoint response profiles does not yet explain why the endpoint
components should be identified as source states. There are two live options:

1. a missing source-authorized constructor connects \(E_0\) and \(E_1\);
2. no such constructor exists, and their equality is specific to the chosen
   response.

The minimal missing theorem is therefore an explicit legal correspondence

\[
E_0\longleftrightarrow E_1
\]

whose source action, Moore-face compatibility, and response invariance are all
derived independently. Atomic simultaneous tail inversion now supplies this
correspondence without passing through either illegal unary intermediate.
